hero.title: Down to the deck.
hero.lede: A full re-roof in eight stages, start to finish. Scroll and watch one: inspection, tear-off, new decking, underlayment, flashing, shingles, ridge, and a storm to prove it.

stages.c: A scan of every course, edge and penetration before anything comes off. Six problems marked.
Old shingles and felt come off down to the boards, straight into the dumpster. Nothing left in the yard.
Every sheet walked and checked. One soft sheet of decking cut out and replaced.
Ice and water shield along the eaves and around the chimney, then synthetic underlayment, lapped from the bottom up.
New drip edge on every edge, step flashing up the chimney, a new boot on the vent pipe.
Laid from the eave up, six nails a shingle, joints staggered so no seam lines up with the one below.
Ridge vent along the peak so the attic breathes, capped with matching ridge shingles.
A real nor'easter is the only inspection that counts. Water sheets off into the gutters; the attic stays dry.

materials.name: Architectural asphalt
materials.blurb: Two laminated layers for depth and shadow. The roof most of Maine is under.

materials.name: Standing-seam metal
materials.blurb: Steel panels with raised, concealed-fastener seams. Snow slides off; it outlasts the house paint twice over.
materials.lay: Panels run eave to ridge, rake to rake, held on hidden clips; each seam locks over the last.
materials.ridge: Vented closure along the peak so the attic breathes, then a matching ridge cap over it.

materials.name: Cedar shake
materials.blurb: Hand-split western red cedar, each one a little different. Weathers to silver in a few seasons.
materials.lay: Hand-split shakes from the eave up, two nails each, a finger-width gap so the wood can swell.
materials.ridge: Ridge vent along the peak so the attic breathes, capped with cedar ridge pieces.

check.title: Repair, or replace?
check.sub: Tick what you can see from the ground or the attic. We'll tell you which way it's leaning and what we'd check first. It's a guide, not a diagnosis: the inspection is free either way.

symptoms.label: Missing or torn shingles
symptoms.hint: Gaps in the pattern, pieces on the lawn after wind
symptoms.check: The seal strips on the courses around the gaps

symptoms.label: Grit in the gutters
symptoms.hint: Sand-like granules collecting at the downspouts
symptoms.check: How much granule cover is left on the sunny side

symptoms.label: Curled or cupped edges
symptoms.hint: Shingle edges lifting or bowing upward
symptoms.check: Attic ventilation, which cooks shingles from below

symptoms.label: A stain on a ceiling
symptoms.hint: Brown rings that grow after rain
symptoms.check: The flashing and boots above the stain, then the decking

symptoms.label: A dip in the roofline
symptoms.hint: The ridge or one side sags between rafters
symptoms.check: Rafters and decking from the attic, before anything else

symptoms.label: Daylight in the attic
symptoms.hint: Pinholes of light through the boards
symptoms.check: Every penetration and the ridge, in daylight from inside

symptoms.label: Moss or black streaks
symptoms.hint: Green clumps or dark stripes down the slope
symptoms.check: Whether the moss has lifted shingles or just stained them

symptoms.label: Hail or a big storm
symptoms.hint: Dents on the gutters, vents or car hoods
symptoms.check: Soft spots and bruising on the shingle mats, by hand

check.note: A ground-level guide only. Hail and wind damage is often invisible from below.
